questions.q: What does the term 'mansab' mean?
options: 'Rank' or 'office'
A land grant given to priests
A tax paid by traders
A treaty between two kingdoms
questions.explanation: Mansab means 'rank' or 'office', and its holders were known as mansabdars. Akbar introduced the mansabdari system, which combined military organisation with civil administration.
questions.fact: Mansab means 'rank' or 'office', and its holders were known as mansabdars.

questions.q: Bābur, who launched the invasion of India in the early 1500s, came from Central Asia and was also known as Zahiruddin Muhammad.
questions.explanation: Zahiruddin Muhammad, also known as Bābur, came from Central Asia. He launched his invasion as the Delhi Sultanate weakened under its last ruler, Ibrāhim Lodī.
questions.fact: Zahiruddin Muhammad, also known as Bābur, from Central Asia launched an invasion on India.

questions.q: During Akbar's siege of Chittor (1567–1568), how long did the Rajputs under Rāṇā Udai Singh resist before the fort was captured?
options: About five days
More than five months
More than five years
They surrendered without fighting
questions.explanation: Under Rāṇā Udai Singh, the Rajputs put up a stiff resistance for more than five months before the fort was captured, and the Mughal army paid a heavy price in the campaign.
questions.fact: Under Rāṇā Udai Singh, the Rajputs put up a stiff resistance for more than five months before the fort was captured.

questions.q: What was the significance of the Battle of Dewair, fought near Udaipur in 1582?
options: It led to the coronation of Chhatrapati Śhivājī
It ended the Ahom kingdom's independence
It resulted in the collapse of key Mughal military outposts in Mewar
It marked the Portuguese conquest of Goa
questions.explanation: The Battle of Dewair (1582) resulted in the collapse of key Mughal military outposts in Mewar and helped Mahārāṇā Pratāp reclaim control over Mewar.
questions.fact: The Battle of Dewair fought near Udaipur in 1582 resulted in the collapse of key Mughal military outposts in Mewar.

questions.q: Under the treaty negotiated between the Mughals and Mewar, what special concession was granted to Mewar's leadership?
options: Control of the port of Surat
The title of Badshah of Hindustan
Freedom from paying any tribute forever
Exemption from personal attendance at the Mughal court
questions.explanation: Under the terms of the treaty, Mewar's leadership was exempted from personal attendance at the Mughal court, which clearly acknowledged Mewar's continued autonomy.
questions.fact: Under the terms of the treaty, Mewar leadership was exempted from personal attendance at the Mughal court.

questions.q: Mewar's state emblem (Coat of Arms) commemorates the Rajput-Bhil alliance. Who is shown at its centre?
options: The Mughal emperor
The goddess Tuljā Bhavānī
Mahārāṇā Pratāp on horseback
The local deity Eklingji (Shiva)
questions.explanation: Mewar's Coat of Arms depicts a Rajput warrior and a Bhil warrior with the local deity Eklingji (Shiva) shown at the centre, commemorating the enduring alliance between the two communities.
questions.fact: Mewar's state emblem depicts a Rajput warrior and a Bhil warrior with the local deity Eklingji (Shiva) shown at the centre.

questions.q: According to poet Dursā Arhā's account, Mahārāṇā Pratāp regularly participated in the Nauroz festival at the Mughal court.
questions.explanation: The poet Dursā Arhā praised Mahārāṇā Pratāp precisely because he never participated in the Nauroz festival nor mounted guard during Jharokha Darshan — signs of his independence from the Mughal court.
questions.fact: You never participated in the Nauroz festival, nor did you mount guard for the imperial presence during Jharokha Darshan.

questions.q: During Akbar's siege of Chittor, Rāṇā Udai Singh retreated to the Aravalli Hills along with a large number of his subjects.
questions.explanation: In a strategic move, Rāṇā Udai Singh retreated to the Aravalli Hills along with a large number of his subjects rather than remain trapped in the fort.
questions.fact: In a strategic move, Rāṇā Udai Singh retreated to the Aravalli Hills along with a large number of his subjects.

questions.q: Mahārāṇā Pratāp fought the Mughal forces in the Battle of Haldighati in the year ___.
questions.explanation: In 1576, Akbar launched another attack on Mewar, and Mahārāṇā Pratāp, son and successor of Rāṇā Udai Singh, fought the Mughal forces in the Battle of Haldighati.
questions.fact: In 1576, Akbar launched another attack on Mewar; Mahārāṇā Pratāp fought against Mughal forces in the Battle of Haldighati.

questions.q: Rānī Abbakkā Chowṭā of Ullal, in present-day Karnataka, defeated the naval forces of the ___.
questions.explanation: Rānī Abbakkā Chowṭā of Ullal (reigned 1525–1570) defeated Portuguese naval forces, showing that resistance to Europeans began soon after their arrival.
questions.fact: 1525–1570: Reign of Rānī Abbakkā Chowṭā of Ullal defeats Portuguese naval forces.

questions.q: Select all correct ways in which the Bhil community strengthened Mahārāṇā Pratāp's resistance.
options: Extensive knowledge of the Aravalli terrain
Command of Mughal artillery units
Expertise in guerrilla warfare
Skills in archery and service as guides
questions.explanation: The Bhils' extensive knowledge of the Aravalli terrain, expertise in guerrilla warfare, skills in archery and role as guides strengthened Mewar's resistance against the Mughals.
questions.fact: Their extensive knowledge of the Aravalli terrain, expertise in guerrilla warfare, skills in archery, role as guides strengthened Mewar's resistance.

questions.q: Which of these statements about Rajput-Mughal relations is INCORRECT?
options: The Kachhwāha Rajputs of Amber, like Mewar, maintained stiff resistance to Mughal authority
The decline of the Delhi Sultanate under Ibrāhim Lodī opened the door to Bābur's invasion
The Mughals needed the Rajputs' military might, loyalty and administrative strength
Some Rajputs were integrated into the empire through grants of mansabs
questions.explanation: Unlike Mewar, the Kachhwāha Rajputs of Amber negotiated cooperative relationships with the Mughals. The other three statements are correct.
questions.fact: Some Rajput kingdoms such as Mewar maintained stiff resistance, while others like the Kachhwāha Rajputs of Amber negotiated cooperative relationships.

questions.q: Arrange these battles in the correct chronological order.
questions.explanation: The correct order is Panipat (1526), Khanua (1527), the siege of Chittor (1567–1568), Haldighati (1576) and finally Dewair (1582).
questions.fact: 1526: Panipat; 1527: Khanua; 1567–68: siege of Chittor; 1576: Haldighati; 1582: Dewair.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Mahārāṇā Pratāp modified his military strategy and adopted guerrilla warfare.
Reason (R): The rugged Aravalli terrain was suited to surprise attacks, raids and ambushes.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.explanation: Mahārāṇā Pratāp used the rugged Aravalli terrain to his advantage, conducting surprise attacks, raids and ambushes on Mughal forces and their networks. The terrain explains why guerrilla warfare worked, so R explains A.
questions.fact: He used the rugged Aravalli terrain to his advantage and conducted surprise attacks, raids, and ambushes on the Mughal forces and their networks.

questions.q: For how long did the Ahom kingdom of Assam maintain its political independence?
options: About a century
Almost six centuries (1228–1826)
About fifty years
Continuously from the 8th century
questions.explanation: The Ahom kingdom of Assam maintained its political independence for almost six centuries (1228–1826) and successfully resisted several invasions and attempts at annexation.
questions.fact: The Ahom kingdom of Assam maintained its political independence for almost six centuries (1228–1826).

questions.q: In 1662, who captured the Ahom capital Garhgaon and imposed a treaty on King Jayadhvaj Singha?
options: Abu Bakr
Mīr Jumlā
Lachit Borphukan
Malik Kāfūr
questions.explanation: In 1662, Mīr Jumlā captured the Ahom capital, Garhgaon, and subsequently a treaty was imposed on King Jayadhvaj Singha.
questions.fact: In 1662, Mīr Jumlā captured the Ahom capital, Garhgaon. Subsequently, a treaty was imposed on King Jayadhvaj Singha.

questions.q: On what did the military strategy of the Ahoms mainly rely?
options: Building the largest cavalry in India
Paying tribute to avoid war
Exploiting the local terrain rather than direct confrontation
Naval battles in the open ocean
questions.explanation: Ahom military strategy relied on exploiting the local terrain rather than engaging in direct confrontation. Their commanders possessed detailed knowledge of Assam's forests, river systems and monsoon cycles.
questions.fact: The military strategy of the Ahoms relied on exploiting the local terrain rather than engaging in direct confrontation.

questions.q: King Jayadhvaj Singha honoured the treaty imposed by the Mughals for the rest of his reign.
questions.explanation: King Jayadhvaj Singha defied the Mughals and renounced the treaty within a year of the Mughal withdrawal, and the Ahoms retained their independence.
questions.fact: The king defied the Mughals and renounced the treaty within a year of the Mughal withdrawal.

questions.q: Despite repeated attempts, the Mughals succeeded in annexing the Brahmaputra valley from the Ahoms.
questions.explanation: Despite repeated attempts by the Mughals to annex the Brahmaputra valley, the Ahoms successfully defended their territories against Mughal invasion.
questions.fact: Despite repeated attempts by the Mughals to annex the Brahmaputra valley, the Ahoms successfully defended their territories against Mughal invasion.

questions.q: The Ahom commander who defeated a Mughal fleet at the Battle of Saraighat in 1671 was ___.
questions.explanation: In 1671, the Ahom commander Lachit Borphukan defeated a Mughal fleet at the Battle of Saraighat, securing the Brahmaputra as an effective territorial boundary.
questions.fact: In 1671, the Ahom commander Lachit Borphukan defeated a Mughal fleet at the Battle of Saraighat.

questions.q: The Ahom navy used light, fast boats called ___, built specifically for river warfare.
questions.explanation: The Ahom navy used light, fast boats called bāchārī, built specifically for river warfare, which gave them an advantage over Mughal fleets.
questions.fact: The Ahom navy used light, fast boats, called bāchārī, built specifically for river warfare.

questions.q: Select all correct components on which Ahom endurance rested.
options: Strategic alliance-building
Building a huge desert cavalry
Guerrilla tactics and Assam's challenging geography
The Paik system of military-administrative organisation
questions.explanation: Ahom endurance rested on a combination of strategic alliance-building, guerrilla tactics, Assam's challenging geography, and the Paik system of military-administrative organisation.
questions.fact: Ahom endurance rested on strategic alliance-building, guerrilla tactics, Assam's challenging geography, and the Paik system.

questions.q: Which of these statements about the Ahom kingdom is INCORRECT?
options: Mughal forces under Abu Bakr made early gains at the first clash but were soon compelled to retreat
The Ahoms retained their independence even after Mīr Jumlā captured Garhgaon
By 1616, the Ahoms had recovered the territory lost in the first clash
At Saraighat, the Ahom commander Lachit Borphukan was defeated by a Mughal fleet
questions.explanation: At the Battle of Saraighat it was Lachit Borphukan who defeated the Mughal fleet, securing the Brahmaputra as a boundary — not the other way around. The other statements are correct.
questions.fact: In 1671, the Ahom commander Lachit Borphukan defeated a Mughal fleet at the Battle of Saraighat.

questions.q: Arrange these Ahom-Mughal events in the correct chronological order.
orderItems: Mīr Jumlā captures the Ahom capital Garhgaon (1662)
questions.explanation: The first Ahom–Mughal clash took place near Samdhara in 1615; by 1616 the Ahoms had recovered the lost territory; Mīr Jumlā captured Garhgaon in 1662; and the Battle of Saraighat followed in 1671.
questions.fact: 1615: first clash near Samdhara; 1616: lost territory recovered; 1662: Garhgaon captured; 1671: Saraighat.

questions.q: Who established the independent kingdom of Vijayanagara in 1336?
options: Kṛiṣhṇadevarāya and Rāma Rāya
Kumāra Kampana and Vīra Ballāla III
Harihara and Bukkā
Malik Kāfūr and Muhammad bin Tughlaq
questions.explanation: Harihara and Bukkā established the independent kingdom of Vijayanagara in 1336, near present-day Hampi in Karnataka, to check the Sultanate's expansion into peninsular India.
questions.fact: Harihara and Bukkā established the independent kingdom of Vijayanagara in 1336.
